record_reviews.summary: Darwin invites Hooker to Down on Saturday the 16th, promises the Phaeton and asks him to bring work; he also plans to invite the Lyells and repeats the transport instruction.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML range is 1 Dec 1846–31 Jan 1847 with exact order unresolved; the editorial note identifies 16 Jan 1847, but this remains a bounded date assessment rather than a single XML day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s four paragraphs survive; the final transport reminder is part of the letter, not an annotation.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Date-crossing logistics letter; no incoming prompt survives in this record.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Hooker for examining the operculum curtain, compares his own Conia sections, says the specimens collapsed, asks to discuss his species sketch and the Norfolk Island flora paper, and mentions the Geological anniversary, Hooker’s visit, and a possible expedition.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 8 Feb 1847; footnotes place Hooker’s visit and Darwin’s Shrewsbury interruption around it.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s seven paragraphs survive; footnotes identify the barnacle and Norfolk flora references but are editorial evidence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The letter begins by answering Hooker’s examination, but that incoming note is absent from this packet; no same-topic candidate is promoted.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Hooker seriatim about Mackinnon’s pamphlet and Sulivan’s address, promises FitzRoy’s statement at the Geological anniversary, postpones his species sketch until Hooker has leisure, and discusses illness in both families.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 17 Feb 1847; the anniversary is 19 Feb and the footnotes support the sequence.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s five paragraphs are complete; editorial notes identify the pamphlets and dates.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The answered note is not preserved here; 1058 is an earlier different letter and is not treated as its prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin proposes an hour or two at 7 Park Street on Wednesday morning, choosing an early breakfast because Hooker rises early.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 28 Feb 1847 from Shrewsbury; no competing date in the body.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s two paragraphs survive as a complete short logistical note.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No substantive prompt; a meeting request alone does not identify an antecedent letter.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker confirms he will come to 7 Park Street on Wednesday but expects to arrive after 9:30; he introduces a Cape-only genus found in Portugal, connects mutation and reversion, and proposes discussing migration and local species change.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 1 Mar 1847; footnote relates it to the 28 Feb and 1 Mar logistics letters and leaves the meeting outcome uncertain.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s two body paragraphs survive; the CD pencil marks in the scholarly sibling are not Hooker’s composition.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Incoming Hooker letter: it supplies the logistical/scientific prompt answered by 1068 only at the meeting-arrangement level.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin says illness prevents him leaving the next day, offers Thursday breakfast instead if Hooker remains in London, and asks Hooker to treat failure to appear by 9 as illness.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 1 Mar 1847; footnote says it is uncertain whether the Thursday meeting occurred.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s two paragraphs are complete and unambiguously his.

evidence.quote: I am so unwell I cannot start from here tomorrow; but if you are still in London, I will come to you to Breakfast on Thursday Morning;
I shall be with you on Wednesday Morning at 7 Park Street but doubt reaching you before 9’30

record_reviews.summary: Hooker’s memorandum starts “Pro” and gives four dense notes on geographically limited natural groups, Epacridaceae/Ericeae and Prionotes, removing providential language, and the geological implications of Kerguelen cabbage; it ends as a note rather than a full letter.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially c. 4 Mar 1847; XML exact day is held because the memorandum may have been forwarded on or shortly after the planned 4 Mar meeting.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker authored the surviving memorandum; the separate annotations are CD pencil marks. Footnotes explicitly say the associated Hooker letter did not survive.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The memorandum itself is the surviving prompt; it is distinct from any missing covering letter.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin says Hooker’s Cape Verde pamphlet arrived, studies “your sheet of notes on my species-sketch,” calls it highly suggestive and a great service, and asks whether Hooker will be at Kew on the 25th or 26th so Darwin can discuss points and ask questions.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 14 Mar 1847; the body and footnote tie “sheet of notes” to the c. 4 Mar memorandum 1066.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s two paragraphs are complete; editorial notes identify the Cape Verde catalogue and the memorandum separately.

evidence.quote: I have studied your sheet of notes on my species-sketch with uncommon interest; they are highly suggestive;
Natural groups having defined limits (sometimes wonderfully so) favourable to local causes effecting change in species.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin proposes a Friday Kew visit, declines the Marquis’s Saturday outing because of his stomach, leaves a Park Street fallback for a breakfast discussion of his sketch, and asks about Hooker’s Indian scheme.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 23 Mar 1847; footnote dates the planned 26 Mar Kew visit, while the body preserves uncertainty about attendance.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s five paragraphs are complete; the Indian-expedition note is editorial context, not a separate voice.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Logistical continuation of the planned discussion; no specific incoming question is preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin cancels the London/Kew trip because of stomach trouble, promises to send his Nulliporae through Reeve to Harvey, and postpones a future Kew visit to April.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 25 Mar 1847; the next-day note and April plan are explicit, but no meeting outcome is claimed.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s four paragraphs survive; footnotes identify Reeve/Harvey and the seaweed material.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Answers Hooker’s missing note of 24 Mar only for logistics/specimens; no preserved candidate input in this packet.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin explains his illness and missed Kew trip, congratulates Hooker’s India prospects, reacts to the clue about Lepidodendron affinities and coal-plant travel, asks to resume the species sketch, sends Nulliporae to Harvey, and asks for examples of rare intermediate varieties.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 7 Apr 1847; footnotes place Hooker’s April field travel and the Reeve/Harvey forwarding in sequence.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s five paragraphs are complete; editorial references to Hooker’s later work do not become contemporary incoming text.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Several requests are Darwin’s own new questions; no incoming prompt is safely identified.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin returns Watson’s letter, challenges the claim that intermediate varieties must be rare, criticizes Hinds’s papers for omitting affinities and habits, mentions Royle, and identifies R. Chambers as the likely author of Vestiges.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 18 Apr 1847; body gives no internal alternative date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s four paragraphs survive; footnote identifies the Watson letter as 12 Apr, which is not itself preserved in this packet.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The explicit Watson input is absent; Hooker is a conduit for the returned letter, so no Hooker prompt is invented.

record_reviews.summary: This two-paragraph preserved extract is Cantor’s 1 May 1847 observation that the Malay Peninsula is zoological neutral ground and that Celebes marks the northern trace of Australian marsupials; Hooker’s covering letter is missing.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The date belongs to Cantor’s extracted letter to William Jackson Hooker, not necessarily to the transmission to Darwin; footnotes explicitly say Hooker copied and enclosed it.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Surviving prose is attributed to T. E. Cantor and presented by Hooker as an extract; it is not Darwin or a complete Hooker letter. CD’s annotations are separate.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Knowledge-only candidate at most: the extract could inform Darwin after receipt, but no receipt date or surviving cover establishes when.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends a geological pamphlet, argues for aquatic/submarine coal and Sigillaria, discusses Henslow’s possible visit and Oxford, accepts Hooker’s Phytologist offer, mentions his wrapped Webb volume and new microscope, and sends compliments to Berkeley.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 1 May 1847; footnotes anchor the pamphlet, Oxford meeting and microscope purchase.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s five paragraphs are complete; the geological claims are his own argument, while cited Brongniart/Binney positions are reported sources.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: It answers Hooker’s missing Cambridge note only in the social/material exchanges; no 1084 prompt is inferred from the shared botany topic.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin explicitly calls the missing Hooker response a “savage onslaught,” then defends his submarine-coal speculation in nine body paragraphs, distinguishing upright from drifted plants and geological from botanical evidence, and asks Hooker to forgive the long defence.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 6 May 1847; the editorial note states Hooker’s letter containing the onslaught has not survived.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s nine paragraphs plus a final thanks paragraph survive; the scholarly CD annotations are separate and the missing Hooker letter cannot be reconstructed.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No in-packet incoming prompt: the actual antecedent is unavailable, so 1087 is not treated as a response to this Darwin letter.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Hooker for his kind note, says he understood the animation behind Hooker’s strong expression, urges him to array facts against aquatic coal, proposes Ehrenberg microscopy and peat/coal ash comparison, and signs before a Geological Council meeting.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 12 May 1847; the council attendance is an editorially corroborated event, not a composition uncertainty.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s three paragraphs are complete; the “kind note” and strong expression refer to a missing Hooker letter, not to Darwin’s own 1086.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The distinctive incoming note is absent; same-correspondent adjacency to 1086 cannot supply it.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks whether Hooker is home and proposes a Friday morning talk, requesting a reply by post; he adds a conditional concern about Sir William’s health.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 22 May 1847; the footnote relates it to the later 25/28 May travel notes.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s three paragraphs are complete.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: A meeting request with no subject does not identify an incoming prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin says he cannot come Friday, offers Thursday for a “jaw,” and asks Hooker to send a line to Park Street if home.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 25 May 1847; footnotes connect it to 1088 and the account-book trip, but do not establish that the meeting occurred.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s three paragraphs are complete; the Falconer phrase is editorially explained.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: A logistical follow-up to Darwin’s own 1088 request, not an incoming Hooker prompt; no reply edge is proposed.

record_reviews.summary: Arranges Darwin’s Friday visit to Kew, declining Hooker’s three beds; it contains no scientific question or answer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The XML gives 17 Nov 1846; the editorial date is exact and pre-period.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s two surviving body paragraphs are his own note; the summary and footnote are editorial.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Pre-period social logistics only; no surviving incoming prompt is answered here.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin praises Hooker’s Galapagos paper, then works through numbered criticisms of St Jago grammar, Compositae counts and distribution, Juan Fernandez–St Helena affinity, Panama/Mexico wording, and the Galapagos table before returning a lens and asking about Elizabeth Hooker.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 23 Nov 1846, pre-period; footnotes date the paper’s Linnean readings later in December but do not move this letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes all body paragraphs; the pencil annotations are CD’s later marks and are not incoming prose.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Pre-period context. The corresponding Hooker answer is 1032 and is already prior-period evidence; no new period prompt is asserted.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker thanks Darwin for revising his paper and answers the St Jago, Compositae, genus/species ratio, Juan Fernandez–St Helena affinity, Panama/Mexico divisions and table criticisms, ending mid-sentence in the preserved fragment.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 24 Nov 1846, pre-period; footnote says it precedes the 1 Dec Linnean reading.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s surviving body is a fragment; separate CD pencil annotations are scholarly marginalia, not Hooker prose.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Pre-period reverse answer to 1031; no new 1847 prompt.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin discusses Hooker’s forced publication/speech, urges him to locate Melville Island coal plants, describes microscopy, encloses a neighbour’s prospectus, thanks him for corallines, and asks after his sister.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorial date is December 1846; outside the packet period.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s eight paragraphs are complete surviving body text; notes identify the Geological Society/Bunbury and coal-plant references.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Pre-period social/scientific context, with no identifiable later prompt in this packet.

proposed_links.reason: The incoming Hooker letter fixes a Wednesday 7 Park Street meeting but predicts arrival after 9:30; Darwin’s same-day note directly changes the plan because illness prevents departure and offers Thursday breakfast if Hooker remains in London. This identifies a logistical reply scope only; the scientific discussion in 1067 is not answered in surviving 1068.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving body, paragraphs 1-2; logistics only.

The editorial note independently identifies 1066 as the memorandum referred to. Scope is the species-sketch discussion in 1071 P1, with P2 logistical.

Several Darwin letters explicitly answer missing Hooker notes; same-author adjacency was not used to reconstruct those inputs.
